title: Buffered provenance can disappear with the workflow
problem: A failed workflow is especially useful to diagnose, but its completed task records may still exist only in process memory.
mechanism: [KNOWN: historical code inspection] Flowcept 1.0.3 offline mode accumulates records in a list and writes them on normal stop or an explicit dump_buffer() call. The timed autoflush settings apply to online mode.
finding: [KNOWN: recorded experiment, 2026-11-11] The stored scenarios show no output file or records after os._exit(9), including after 200 finished tasks, or self-directed SIGTERM. Normal completion and a raised task exception preserved records. These results concern unflushed offline buffers, not broker-backed mode. The lab README separately reports that a manual dump before SIGTERM preserved 200 records; that workaround is not one of the six stored scenarios. This is a documented design limit, not an undocumented durability promise.

experiment.limitations: Historical results, not rerun for this card. Reproduction requires Python with Flowcept 1.0.3 installed. Recorded environment: Python 3.11.15, macOS arm64. Synthetic offline workflows only; no broker, adapter, thread or async tests. The scenarios named hard_kill use os._exit(9), not external SIGKILL. The command prints new summaries and does not overwrite the stored result file.

adaptation: [INFERRED] When building an agent runner, explicitly choose the acceptable telemetry loss window and test termination after useful work has finished. Periodic persistence or durable append-only recording may reduce loss; measure recovery and overhead before claiming durability.
unknowns: Durability and failure behavior of Flowcept online modes were not measured here.
Behavior under external SIGKILL, host power loss, disk failure and concurrent instrumentation is untested.
Whether a later Flowcept revision changes offline persistence requires fresh inspection.
